title: Studying the Possibilities of Creating Artificial Clouds and Rain
content: The results of experimental and theoretical studies into possibility of creating artificial clouds and rain by stimulating convection based on the following physical principles are discussed: 1) heating of local areas of the surface layer of the atmosphere by artificial aerosol layer that absorbs solar radiation; 2) creation of an updraft along a 30-40 tier garland of black screens lifted on a balloon and warmed by the sun; 3) conducting into the atmosphere a vertically directed high-speed jet fueled by the heat of water vapor condensation on three types of aerosols with different hygroscopic points. The performance of these three methods was evaluated on the basis of theoretical modeling and field experiments. It is shown that the application of the first method requires the creation of an optically dense aerosol layer over an area of about 5-10 km2, existing for at least 30 minutes. This requires such large dosages of aerosol compositions that the application of this method is expensive and acceptable due to atmospheric pollution only in desert areas. Theoretical modeling and experimental testing of the second method showed its complete futility because the large sailing of the screens does not allow to lift the garland having more than 4-5 tiers even in low wind, secondly, adiabatic cooling and wind drift excludes the formation of a continuous updraft flow by adding the updraft pulses created by each tier. Field tests in the UAE of the jet method fueled by condensation heat have shown the possibility of creating small clouds and localized short-term rains. But these results are much lower than theoretically expected. The reason for this is that the air humidity on the days with the experiments was below the hygroscopic point of the two types of aerosols introduced into the jet at the start, secondly, the condensation process is not so fast to provide energy feeding of the jet during its ascent, and the power of the applied aircraft engine D-30 is insufficient to overcome the surface layers of inversion and the destructive effect of wind. Based on these results, it is proposed to use much more powerful aerospace engines with some modernization, the jet of which, rising into the atmosphere, can provide the formation of a powerful convective cloud of the Cb type. To accelerate precipitation formation, a hygroscopic nano-aerosol in the required concentration is introduced into this cloud at a height of 400-500 m using a UAV.
